name: Focusmate
tagline: Scheduled one-to-one virtual coworking sessions for accountability

pricing.notes: Official pricing page reviewed; taxes, promotions, and regional pricing may differ.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Custom team programme; no public numeric price or usage cap.

pricing.hiddenCosts: The $8 figure on file is the annual-billing equivalent; month-to-month Plus is $12. Applicable taxes can be added at checkout.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Focusmate's durable value is polish, OS integration, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local desktop utility that captures the essential virtual coworking workflow with keyboard-first controls and local storage.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: macOS, Windows, or Linux development machine
Local filesystem access and OS permissions
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: bank, payment, tax, and reconciliation integrations
whyPeopleStillPay: Focusmate: People keep paying because a utility used dozens of times a day must be instant, predictable, and compatible with every OS update.
ongoingBurden: Track OS permission changes, shortcut conflicts, packaging, code signing, and regressions after system updates.

priorArt.name: ActivityWatch
priorArt.desc: Local-first automatic time tracking with an extensible event model.

alternatives.name: Focus101
alternatives.desc: One matched body-double per workday on the free plan; weekends must fend for themselves.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Cofocus
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The right format, but the free plan stops at three sessions a week.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Flow Club
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A group coworking service with a trial, not a free plan and not one-to-one.

rejectedAlternatives.name: FocusPair
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Free video coworking, provided you already have a partner; matching and scheduling are absent.

notes: Credibility row: Focusmate survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Focusmate; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local desktop utility that captures the essential virtual coworking workflow with keyboard-first controls and local storage.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: deep operating-system edge-case coverage; polished shortcuts and accessibility; vendor-maintained updates.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
